name: Session 1 - Services Marketing
summary:
{%:Introduction}

The macro-environment change the ways in which service firms do business. Services marketing differ from goods marketing, because a service is an act or performance rather than an object and there is an expanded marketing mix (7Ps) for services. In this session, we aim to understand how services differ from goods and understand challenges that face service marketers due to these distinct differences. 

{%} {%:Guidelines}

- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

- Understand the significance of services.

- Define what characterises a service.

- Identify key characteristics that distinguish services from goods.

- Categorise a service in different ways.

- Identify key components of a service system.

- Describe the expanded ‘marketing mix’ for services.

{%}{%:Resources}Essential textbook:

- Chapter 1 (An overview of Services Marketing): Lovelock, C., Patterson, P., Wirtz, J., 2011, Services Marketing: An Asia-Pacific and Australian Perspective, Sixth Edition, Pearson Australia. (ISBN 9781486002702) 

{%}

name: Session 2 - Understanding Service Consumers
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Consumer behaviour differs between goods and services, especially so at the purchase and consumption stages. These behavioural differences can be better understood through different theories of behaviour. In this session, we aim to understand how customers react in service encounters and the importance of understanding customers’ behaviours for service marketers. 

{%}{%:Guidelines}

- Read relevant textbook chapters.

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions.

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions.

{%}{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to: 

- Understand the three-stage model of service consumption.

- Learn why consumers often have difficulty evaluating services, especially those with many experience and credence attributes.

- Know the perceived risks customers face in purchasing services and the strategies firms can use to reduce consumer risk perceptions.

- Understand how customers form service expectations and the components of these expectations.

- Understand the “moment of truth” metaphor.

- Contrast how customers experience and evaluate high- versus low-contact services.

- Obtain insights from viewing the service encounter as a form of theater.

- Know how role, script, and perceived control theories contribute to a better understanding of service encounters.

- Describe how customers evaluate services and what determines their satisfaction.

- Understand service quality, its dimensions and measurement, and how quality relates to customer loyalty.

- Know why customer loyalty is such an important outcome of excellent service experiences.

{%}{%:Resources}Essential textbook:

- Chapter 2

name: Session 3 - Positioning Services in Competitive Markets
summary:
{%:Introduction}

To succeed in a competitive environment, service providers have to set themselves apart from competitors through positioning. In this session, we understand how market segmentation works and how to define target markets. We outline how positioning maps can be used as a tool to develop a competitive strategy.

{%} {%:Guidelines}

- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions

{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

- Understand how customer, competitor, and company analyses (i.e., the 3 Cs) help to develop a customer-driven services marketing strategy.

- Know the key elements of a positioning strategy (i.e., STP) and explain why they are so crucial for service firms.

- Segment customers on the basis of needs before using other common bases to further identify and profile the segments.

- Distinguish between important and determinant attributes for segmentation.

- Position a service to distinguish it from its competitors.

{%} {%:Resources}Essential textbook:

- Chapter 3

{%}

name: Session 4 - Developing Service Products
summary:
{%:Introduction} This chapter introduces the idea of a service product, which is different from physical goods because it is mostly experienced rather than owned. A well-defined service product helps customers understand its value, branding, pricing, and how to buy it. The chapter explains the three key parts of a service product: the core service (what customers are actually buying), supplementary services (extra features that support and enhance the service), and the delivery process (how the service is provided). It also introduces the Flower of Service, which shows how different supporting services help improve the customer experience. Branding is an important topic, as it helps make services stand out, builds customer trust, and creates loyalty. {%}

{%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

- Understand what a service product is and why defining it clearly is important.

- Identify the three components of a service product.

- Explain the Flower of Service model and how supplementary services enhance the core product.

- Recognize the role of branding in services, including brand architecture and brand equity.

- Understand how companies develop new services, from small improvements to major innovations.

- Apply design thinking to service design and identify key factors for success. {%} 

{%:Resources}Essential Textbook:

Chapter 4

name: Session 5 - Service Distribution
summary:
{%:Introduction}This session highlights some of the key distinctions between distributing a service and distributing a physical good, emphasizing the role of time and place and the opportunity to distribute information-based services in cyberspace through electronic rather than physical channels.{%}

{%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters.

{%:Learning Outcomes}

- Understand the four foundational questions—What? How? Where? When?—that shape service distribution strategy.

- Describe the three types of flows that define what is being distributed in service delivery.

- Recognize the three main ways services can be distributed and the distinction between core and supplementary services.

- Identify the challenges of delivering services online and the factors driving digital service growth.

- Understand the factors influencing customers' choices of service delivery channels.

- Recognize why integrating different service channels is crucial for a seamless customer experience.

- Describe how service locations are chosen strategically and tactically.

- Understand the factors influencing the extension of service hours.

- Assess the role, benefits, and costs of intermediaries in service delivery.

- Explain why franchising is a widely used model for delivering services to end customers.{%}

{%:Resources}Essential textbook:

Chapter 5 {%}

name: Session 6 - Setting Prices and Implementing Revenue Management
summary:
{%:Introduction} The foundations of pricing include different types of costs and the development of pricing objectives. In this session, we aim to understand how service marketers formulate pricing strategies and use revenue management practices. This session also helps understand how to balance demand and supply using capacity management. Demand management strategies are critical for service products perishable in nature. {%}

{%:Guidelines}

- Read online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions.

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities. {%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

-          Understand that pricing is vital to a service firm's financial success.

-          Learn the pricing tripod—costs, value, and competition—as the basis of pricing strategy.

-          Know different types of costs and the limits of cost-based pricing.

-          Grasp the idea of net value and how to improve it by adding value or reducing costs.

-          Explore how competition affects pricing and when markets are less price-driven.

-          Understand how revenue management helps maximise income.

-          Recognise how rate fences support effective revenue strategies.

-          Be aware of ethical issues and customer concerns around pricing.

-          Learn how to make revenue policies feel fair to consumers.

-          Identify six key questions to design a strong pricing strategy. {%}

{%:Resources}

Chapter 6 {%}

name: Session 7: Promoting Services and Educating Customers
summary:
{%:Introduction}

Marketing communications is often seen as short-term tactics like advertising or promotions. In this session, we take a broader view by exploring how communications support long-term brand-building in services. We look at a range of tools available to service marketers and discuss the unique challenges—such as intangibility and customer involvement—that communication strategies must address. {%}

{%:Guidelines}

- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions.{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}

By the end of this session you will be able to:

By the end of this session, you will be able to:

- Understand the 5 Ws of service communication: Who, What, How, Where, and When.

- Identify the main audiences for service communication.

- Explain key communication goals and messages.

- Understand the service communication funnel.

- Describe the roles communication can play in services.

- Recognize common challenges and how to overcome them.

- Know the main communication tools and channels.

- Understand how digital tools support communication.

- Identify messages delivered during service and from outside the firm.

- Know when to communicate and how to plan and measure it.

- Be aware of ethics and privacy in communication.

- Understand the role of branding and design.

- See why integrated communication is important for brand success. {%}

{%:Resources} Essential textbook:

Chapters 7 {%}

{%:Introduction}Service marketers use integrated marketing communications (IMC) to deliver a consistent message to customers. It is important to ensure that all communications deliver a strong brand identity. What is being communicated to customers has an impact on customers’ expectations and perceived service quality. In this session, we aim to understand how IMC strategy can be developed for services.{%}

{%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters.

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions.

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions.{%} {%:Learning Outcomes}- Understand the importance and difficulties of IMC in services.

- Identify the 5Ws of marketing communications planning.

- Be familiar with the marketing communication mix.{%} {%:Resources}Essential textbook:

Chapter 8 (An overview of Services Marketing): Lovelock, C., Patterson, P., Wirtz, J., 2011, Services Marketing: An Asia-Pacific and Australian Perspective, Sixth Edition, Pearson Australia.

name: Session 8 - Designing Service Processes
summary:
{%:Introduction} This session focuses on designing and managing service processes from the customer’s point of view. It introduces service blueprints as a vital tool for visualising and analysing service interactions, enabling more effective process redesign. The chapter also explores the customer's role as a co-producer in the service experience, highlighting how their participation shapes outcomes. In addition, the increasing adoption of self-service technologies (SSTs) is discussed, along with their impact on service delivery and customer involvement. {%}

{%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

- Distinguish between a service experience and a service process.
- Compare flowcharting and service blueprinting. Create a service blueprint with standard design elements.
- Use fail-proofing to eliminate process fail points.
- Set service standards and performance targets.
- Consider customer perceptions and emotions in design.
- Understand why service process redesign is necessary.
- Link redesign to improved quality and productivity.

- Identify levels of customer participation.
- Explain customers as co-creators of value.
- Examine what influences acceptance of SSTs.
- Manage reluctance to adopt new service behaviours.
- Explore the impact of service robots and AI.
- Distinguish robots from traditional SSTs.
- Match service types to employees, robots, or hybrid teams.

{%}

{%:Resources}Essential textbook:

Chapter 8 {%}

name: Session 9 - Crafting the Service Environment
summary:
{%:Introduction} This session looks at how the service environment shapes customer perceptions and supports the overall service experience. It introduces the servicescape model, which explains how physical surroundings affect both customers and employees. The chapter highlights that good service design should not only look and feel appealing but also help customers move easily through the service process. {%}

{%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

- Understand the four main purposes of service environments.
- Learn how people react to service spaces using ideas from psychology.
- Get to know the servicescape model and how it works.
- Identify the three key parts of a service environment.
- Explore how lighting, sound, and scent affect customers.
- See how space layout and how things work influence service flow.
- Understand how signs and objects send messages to customers.
- Recognise how staff and other customers shape the environment.
- Learn why servicescape design must consider the whole experience from the customer’s view.

{%}

{%:Resources}Essential textbook: 

Chapter 10 {%}

name: Session 10 - Managing People for Service Advantage
summary:
{%:Introduction} This session focuses on how human resource management drives service excellence. It highlights the critical role of frontline employees as brand ambassadors and explores the challenges they face in delivering quality service. The Service Talent Cycle is introduced to show how hiring, training, and motivating staff can shift a firm from a Cycle of Failure to a Cycle of Success. The session also emphasises the importance of building a strong service culture and having value-driven leadership. {%}

{%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

Explain why service employees are key to a firm's success.
- Understand why frontline jobs are often stressful and demanding.
- Describe the cycles of failure, mediocrity, and success in service HR.
- Learn the main steps of the Service Talent Cycle.
- Know how to find and hire the right service staff.
- Identify what training service employees need.
- Understand the value of internal communication.
- Explain why empowering frontline staff matters.
- Learn how to build strong service teams.
- Understand what a service-focused culture looks like.
- Tell the difference between service climate and culture.
- Recognise what makes a great service leader. {%}

{%:Resources}Essential textbook: 

Chapter 11 {%}

name: Session 11 - Managing Relationships and Building Loyalty
summary:
{%:Introduction} This session introduces how firms can develop a loyal and profitable customer base. It introduces the Wheel of Loyalty, which shows three systematic steps in building customer loyalty. Starting with the foundations for loyalty (including segmentation, selective customer acquisition, tiering of service, and service quality), it shows how to create loyalty bonds (including deepening the relationship through cross- selling and bundling, loyalty rewards, and higher-level social, customization, and structural bonds).{%}

 {%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Watch online resources and answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.

- Test self-knowledge on 3 post-workshop MCQ questions.{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:

- Understand how customer loyalty increases a firm’s profits.
- Know why customers stay loyal to a service brand.
- Identify key loyalty strategies in the Wheel of Loyalty.
- Recognise the need to focus on the right target customers.
- Use service tiering to manage and retain customers.
- Link customer satisfaction to long-term loyalty.
- Strengthen loyalty through cross-selling and bundling.
- Use both financial and non-financial rewards to build loyalty.
- Build deeper bonds through social, personalised, and structural connections.
- Understand why customers leave and how to reduce switching. {%}

{%:Resources}

Essential textbook:

name: Session 12 - Improving Service Quality and Productivity
summary:
{%:Introduction} 

This session introduces the concept of service quality and how to measure and improve it. Students will learn about the gap model, which helps identify where quality shortfalls occur, and explore tools and strategies to close these gaps. The session also highlights the link between quality and productivity, stressing that firms must work to improve both together to stay competitive.

{%} {%:Guidelines}- Read relevant textbook Chapters

- Answer the pre-workshop questions

- Attend the workshop seminar. Work and participate in discussion on pre-workshop questions and workshop activities.{%}

{%:Learning Outcomes}By the end of this session you will be able to:
- Understand how service quality, productivity, and profits are connected.
- Learn different ways people view service quality.
- Use the Gaps Model to find and fix quality issues.
- Know the difference between hard (measurable) and soft (perception-based) quality metrics.
- Understand the purpose of collecting customer feedback.
- Learn tools used to gather customer feedback.
- Be familiar with using control charts and hard data to track quality.
- Choose the right tools to analyse service problems.
- Learn what return on quality means and how reliable service should be.
- Define and measure service productivity.
- Know the difference between being productive, efficient, and effective.
- Identify ways to boost service productivity.
- Understand how improving productivity affects quality and customer value. {%}

{%:Resources}Essential textbook:
